---
title: "Showcase: Na-22 511 keV Coincidence with LBC Detectors"
format: gfm
---

Follow a completed two-detector measurement from the physical arrangement and
511 keV energy selection to CFD timing and coincidence energy matrices. Both
sessions can be replayed without a connected digitizer.

**Dataset:** [Na-22 511 keV coincidence measurements with LBC scintillators:
CFD timing and replayable EWT Digitizer sessions](https://zenodo.org/records/23667120).
**Version DOI:** [10.5281/zenodo.23667120](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667120).
The measurements were recorded on **26 October 2026** with **nlab 0.7.7**.

## 1. Understand the experiment

Two cylindrical **25C25-LBC scintillators**, each nominally **1 inch in diameter
and 1 inch long**, were coupled to **R13089 PMTs**. Their signals were connected
to CH0 and CH1 of one Digitizer 4.0. Both PMT high-voltage settings were
**1000 V**. The active PMT divider is shown in the photograph below.

![Active PMT divider used with the R13089 PMT. Original experiment
photograph.](images/showcase-na22-divider.jpg){width=420}

The **POLATOM Na-22 source** has a reference activity of **330 kBq on
26 June 2023**. That date belongs to the activity specification; the measurements
were made in October 2026.

| Arrangement | Physical placement | Dataset label |
|---|---|---|
| Close | Detector housings placed as close together as practical | `0cm` / `close` |
| Offset source | Source 15 cm from the left detector and 5 cm from the right detector | `15cm` |

The `15cm` label describes the source placement in the second arrangement. Use
both source-to-detector distances when describing this geometry.

![Close arrangement: the two detector housings face each other with the smallest
practical gap. Original experiment photograph.](images/showcase-na22-setup-close.jpg)

![Offset-source arrangement: the source is 15 cm from the left detector and 5 cm
from the right detector. Original experiment photograph.](images/showcase-na22-setup-offset.jpg)

## 2. Recognize the photopeak selection and timing settings

The coincidence measurement selected an energy region around the **511 keV
annihilation photopeak on each channel**. In the MCA workspace, the shaded ROI
shows the selected pulse-height region. Its coordinates are raw MCA channels;
different detector gains put the same photon energy at different positions.

![Recorded MCA view of the close arrangement, showing the CH1 photopeak ROI,
CFD controls, and diagnostic waveforms. The horizontal spectrum axis is raw MCA
channel.](images/showcase-na22-mca.png)

The acquisition-start records retain these applied energy bounds:

| Arrangement | CH0 ROI, MCA channels | CH1 ROI, MCA channels |
|---|---|---|
| Close | 1035–1196 | 1697–1888 |
| Offset source | 1054–1214 | 1772–1964 |

These bounds describe this dataset's gain and processing settings. For a new
measurement, locate the photopeak independently on each detector.

| Coincidence setting | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Logic | CH0 AND CH1 |
| Energy gates | Both channel ROIs enabled |
| Timing | CFD fine |
| CFD fraction and delay | Approximately 0.40; 16 ns |
| Accepted time difference | −48 ns to +48 ns |
| Difference convention | CH1 event time minus CH0 event time |
| Applied channel-delay correction | 0 ns |
| Timing-histogram bin width | 62.5 ps |
| Delayed-random sidebands | Enabled |

The bin width specifies histogram sampling. The measured peak width describes
the full detector and electronics setup under these conditions. See
[Coincidence Measurement](coincidence) for timing conventions, pair counting,
and the Gaussian-core fit.

## 3. Download and replay the close arrangement

The Zenodo record provides a flat file list. The numerical sessions are stored
in two `.7z` archives; photographs, screenshots, a settings snapshot, and the
dataset README can also be downloaded individually.

| Arrangement | Download | Session directory after extraction |
|---|---|---|
| Close | [2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_close.7z](https://zenodo.org/records/23667120/files/2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_close.7z?download=1) | `2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_close/session_20261026_125809.nlab-session/` |
| Offset source | [2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_15cm.7z](https://zenodo.org/records/23667120/files/2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_15cm.7z?download=1) | `2026_10_26_PMT_LBC_15cm/session_20261026_134341.nlab-session/` |

1. Install **nlab 0.7.7** or a later release compatible with these sessions.
   The application requires the platform-appropriate drivers and native runtime
   from [Analog Devices libiio v0.26](https://github.com/analogdevicesinc/libiio/releases/tag/v0.26).
   On Windows, the release provides `libiio-0.26.ga0eca0d2-setup.exe`.
   Follow [Getting Started](getting_started) for application installation.
2. Download the close-arrangement archive and extract it with a 7z-compatible
   tool. Preserve all five files inside the `.nlab-session` directory.
3. Launch the application, select **two channels**, and choose
   **Offline / Replay Mode** in the startup dialog.
4. Choose **File -> Replay Session...** and select the extracted close session
   directory shown above. The application validates the finalized capture.
5. Open **MCA** to follow recorded histogram and diagnostic checkpoints. Open
   **Coincidence -> Timing and spectra** to follow the reconstructed timing
   histogram and participating-event spectra.
6. Let playback finish. The close bundle spans approximately **296.55 s**, with
   about **243.1 s** between the coincidence start and finish events. Watch the
   replay completion status; the final plots remain on screen.

The window identifies offline/replay operation and hardware acquisition remains
disabled. Session playback uses recorded host timing, including the intervals
before and after coincidence acquisition. The recorded setup photographs and
screenshots illustrate acquisition; their historical connection titles describe
the original measurement workstation.

## 4. Read the timing result and compare the second arrangement

The top plot shows the signed CH1-minus-CH0 time difference. The lower spectra
show the energy distributions of participating events. Read the applied ROI
bounds, pair counters, fit-quality message, and fitted curve together.

![Archived close-arrangement timing screenshot after drain. Both 511 keV ROIs
are enabled. The footer reports a non-Gaussian/poor-fit warning.](images/showcase-na22-timing-close.png)

Choose **File -> Exit Replay Mode**, then load the offset-source session from
the second archive. This bundle spans approximately **886.48 s**, including
about **881.6 s** of coincidence acquisition. Wait for the same completion
status before comparing the final views.

![Archived offset-source timing screenshot after drain, with both 511 keV ROIs
enabled and the Gaussian-core fit displayed.](images/showcase-na22-timing-offset.png)

The supplied screenshots report:

| Arrangement | Fitted centre | Gaussian-core FWHM | Reduced chi-square | Displayed fit quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Close | +0.069 ns | 393 ± 1 ps | 60.98 | Non-Gaussian / poor fit |
| Offset source | +0.421 ns | 442 ± 3 ps | 2.21 | Gaussian-core fit |

These numbers are transcribed from the archived screenshots. In particular, the
close run's small formal width uncertainty accompanies a poor-fit warning; it
does not include the effect of that model mismatch. Inspect the peak shape and
fit message before comparing widths. A channel-delay correction of zero also
means the fitted centres retain the setup's relative timing offsets.

The two acquisition intervals differ substantially. Compare widths and shapes
under the documented selections; total pair counts alone do not compare
coincidence efficiency between the arrangements. The intervals above are host
elapsed times, without a dead-time correction.

## 5. Explore the energy matrix

Open **Coincidence -> Energy matrix**. CH0 energy is on the horizontal axis and
CH1 energy is on the vertical axis. The projections show energy populations
within the movable display gates. Raw MCA channels remain the coordinate system
unless a valid energy calibration supplies energy labels.

Use the display's **Prompt**, **Delayed random**, and **Prompt - scaled random**
selections to inspect the corresponding matrices. The random estimate uses the
two recorded sidebands, scaled by 0.5 before subtraction. Linear/logarithmic
scales and projection gates change the matrix presentation.

![Archived close-arrangement prompt energy matrix and projections. Both MCA ROI
gate options are unchecked in this screenshot, showing a broader energy
selection.](images/showcase-na22-energy-matrix.png)

This supplied matrix screenshot shows both energy gates off. The sessions'
recorded coincidence settings enable the 511 keV ROIs, so their replayed matrix
has the stored energy selection. Keep that selection difference in mind when
comparing the archived figure with replay. Details of matrix axes, projection
gates, and random subtraction are in [Coincidence Measurement](coincidence).
